blocks.text: Dear Ms. Frazier:

Thank you for the two long conversations this spring, and for how candid you were in both of them. A board seat is a harder brief than a management role, and you told us plainly what the last eighteen months have asked of your directors. That helps us more than a job description would. This letter sets out the terms on which we will conduct the search for the independent director your board intends to seat. We have written it in plain language and we mean it to be the whole of our agreement on this work. Where a term matters to you and reads wrong, telephone me before you sign it and we will settle it between us.
What We Are Engaged to Do

We will conduct a retained search for one independent director for the board of {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}. The work runs from the written specification through to the appointment. We agree the brief with you, map the market it sits in, approach candidates in confidence, assess them against the brief, present a slate, take references on the finalists, and stay with you through the board's decision and the invitation. We are retained for the search itself and are not paid on placement. Our obligation is to bring you the field and to tell you honestly what we think of it.

Some work sits outside this letter. We are not conducting a governance review, we are not benchmarking board compensation, and we are not searching for management roles. Each of those is available to you under a separate engagement. If this search turns up a question of that kind, and board searches often do, we will raise it with you and wait for your instruction before we begin any of it.
How We Will Run It

Our method is deliberate at the front and quick at the back. We spend the first weeks on the specification, because everything after it is measured against that document, and a seat filled against a vague brief tends to be filled again. The search then runs in four stages, and you will know at any moment which of them we are in.

items: 1. Specification. We interview your board members and the executives a new director would work alongside, and we write a specification that states the purpose of the seat, the experience it requires, and the committee work it carries. Nothing goes to a candidate until you have approved that document.

2. Market map. We chart the companies and sectors where the experience you want actually sits, and we build the long list from that map instead of from a contact book. You will see the map, so that you can tell us where we have looked in the wrong place.

3. Approach and assessment. Our consultants make the approaches themselves, by telephone and in confidence. We assess each candidate against the specification and keep a written record of every conversation, and we do not carry anyone forward on enthusiasm alone.

4. Slate and references. We present the slate in person and take the board through it as a group. References are taken on the finalists only, with the candidate's consent, and we report what we hear without softening it.

blocks.text: The People on Your Search

Jeffrey Patterson, a Research Consultant with this firm, carries the search day to day and is your first call on anything that will not wait. James Grant, our Senior Consultant on the engagement, runs the assessment conversations and will sit with you when the slate is presented. Jason Bell, Research Associate, builds the market map and the long list and makes the first calls into the market. I read everything that leaves this firm on your search, and I am accountable to you for all of it.
Fees and Payment

Our fee for this search is {{fact:f:E-2017-001.fee}}, fixed, and it does not move with the compensation of the director you appoint. We commence work on {{fact:f:E-2017-001.start}}, subject to your signature on this letter. We bill the fee in three equal installments: the first on commencement, the second when the slate is presented, and the third on appointment or at the close of the search, whichever comes first. Out-of-pocket expenses, which on a search of this kind means candidate travel and our own, are billed at cost with the invoice for the period in which they fall. Invoices are payable within thirty days of their date.
Term and Termination

This agreement takes effect on the date you sign below and continues until the search closes and our final invoice is paid. Either of us may end it earlier on written notice to the other. If you end it, you owe us the fee earned to that point together with expenses incurred, and we will hand over the specification, the market map, and the candidate record as they stand, so that whoever takes the work on is not starting from nothing. If the director we place leaves the board within twelve months for a reason other than a change in the board's own composition, we will conduct one replacement search for expenses only.
Confidentiality and Discretion

We will hold what you tell us in confidence and use it only for this engagement. Inside the firm, access is limited to the people named above and to the administrative staff whose work on the search requires it. We will not disclose your information outside the firm without your consent, except where a court or another authority with jurisdiction compels it, and in that event we will tell you first if we are free to. Discretion runs in the other direction as well, and it is the part of this business we are strictest about: candidates are described to you by their current role and their record, and their names are used only in the slate document and in the room where it is discussed. For the life of this engagement and for twelve months after it closes, we will not approach anyone employed by {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} for this or any other search.
Limitation of Liability

Our liability to you arising out of this engagement, however it is framed, will not exceed the total fees you pay us under it, except in the case of our fraud or willful misconduct. Neither of us will be liable to the other for indirect or consequential loss, including lost profits or lost opportunity. We take references, verify credentials, and report to you what we find. The appointment itself is the board's decision to make, and we do not warrant how any director will perform once seated.
Governing Law

This agreement is governed by the law of the state in which this firm keeps its principal office, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. If a dispute arises between us, each of us will put someone with authority to settle it on a call before either begins a proceeding. This letter and its signature page are the entire agreement between us on their subject, and either may be changed only in a writing signed by both of us.

If all of this matches your understanding, please sign both copies of the signature page, keep one for your file, and return the other to my office. If any of it does not, telephone me and we will put it right before you sign anything. The one thing I need from you now is the signed letter. When it reaches me we will book the specification interviews with your board and begin.
With warm regards,
Kickoff: board director search, {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}

To: Jeffrey Patterson, James Grant
From: Jason Bell
Copy: engagement file

The engagement opened {{fact:f:E-2017-001.start}}. The board is seating one independent director and the seat is weighted to audit committee work. This memo records the objective, the five pieces of work, who owns each, and what I need this week.
Objective

Present a slate of independent directors who can serve on the audit committee from their first meeting. The client wants financial depth and someone who has seen a company through a change of scale. Sector adjacency is desirable and not required.

The intake call set two constraints worth repeating here. The board meets four times a year and expects committee work between meetings, so availability is a screening question and not a closing one. And the seat is being added, not replaced, which means there is no predecessor for a candidate to be measured against.
The work
Five pieces, listed in the order they gate one another. Nothing downstream of the specification begins before the client has signed it off.

items: 1. Specification. Interviews with Jennifer Frazier and with the nominating committee, then a draft for their approval. Jeffrey Patterson leads. Nothing goes to a candidate before it is signed off.

2. Market map. Companies in the client's revenue band plus two adjacent sectors, and separately the population of sitting and former audit chairs. I own this. Target is a map we can defend rather than a long one.
3. Long list. Built from the map and not from the files. I own it. James Grant reads it before any name is approached.

4. Approach protocol. Every approach by telephone and by a consultant. James Grant sets the wording. No candidate name travels outside the engagement file, and the client sees roles and records until the slate.
5. Reporting. A written update to Jennifer Frazier every two weeks and a working session with the client at each review point. Jeffrey Patterson owns the client relationship. I draft.

blocks.text: Timing

The specification should be signed off inside three weeks. The map runs alongside it and does not wait for it. The first formal approaches follow the client review of the long list and not before, which puts them a clear month out on the current shape of the calendar.
Open questions

Two things are unresolved and both affect the approach wording. We do not know whether the seat carries the audit committee chair or only membership, and candidates at this level will ask before they agree to a conversation. We also do not know how the board wants the search described if a candidate's own employer hears about it, which on a board seat is a live possibility and not a remote one.

Both belong in the specification interview and not in a note. They are short questions and they will take two minutes in the room, and the answers are worth more when we can hear the hesitation behind them.
This week

The specification interviews are the gate on everything else, so scheduling them is the first job. I will send the request to Jennifer Frazier today and hold two slots that suit James Grant as well, since he should hear the brief first hand rather than read it.
Jeffrey Patterson, the draft outline for the specification is yours. My notes from the intake call are in the engagement file and they are fuller than the summary I sent round.

James Grant, I need your read on the approach wording before I make any research calls. I will not put a call into the market until it is settled. If you want the first version to come from me, say so and I will draft it against the intake notes.
Good morning Jennifer,

Two weeks on from the specification sign-off, here is where the {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} board search stands. The market map is finished and the long list closed at forty-one names, drawn from your revenue band and the two adjacent sectors we agreed. Research calls are underway to test which of those names would take a board conversation this summer. Nine of those calls are done. The early read is strong on operating background and thinner on audit committee experience, which is roughly what we expected from the map.

No formal approach goes out until we have read the list with you. I would like to book that session for the last week of the month, ninety minutes, with whoever from the nominating committee can attend. Send me two or three windows and I will work around them. I will circulate the list by sector a couple of days beforehand so that nobody is reading it cold in the room.

One point needs settling before the approaches begin. The specification says the seat carries audit committee work, and candidates will ask whether it carries the chair. The answer changes who says yes. If the committee has a view, even a provisional one, I will fold it into the approach note. Jeffrey is copied and can pick anything up while I am on calls.
Sincerely,
Working session on the {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}} board search

The session was called to read the long list name by name and to settle which of those names we approach, and this record follows the order the meeting took: who was present, where the search stands, what we settled, the reservations that were voiced, and the items each of us now carries.
Present

items: James Grant, Senior Consultant
Jeffrey Patterson, Research Consultant
Jason Bell, Research Associate
Jennifer Frazier, Chief Operating Officer, {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}

blocks.text: Where the search stands

Jason Bell reported that the long list closed at forty-one names, built off the market map and tested since by research calls rather than by any formal approach, and that of the forty-one he would expect roughly half to take a board conversation in the next few weeks, with the audit committee requirement accounting for most of the balance. He took the room through the map by sector before the names, which was the right order, because two of the sectors we had assumed would carry candidates turned out to be thin once the revenue band was applied.

Jennifer Frazier answered the question we had put to her ahead of the session. The seat carries audit committee membership from the first meeting, and the committee has not yet decided whether it carries the chair. She asked that we approach on membership and treat the chair as open, and she undertook to bring the question back to us once the committee has met.
What we settled

Fourteen of the forty-one are carried forward for approach, taken in priority order, with the priority set by the fit to the specification and not by how likely a name is to answer. The remaining twenty-seven stay on the list and Jason Bell continues research calls against them, so that the list behind the fourteen is live if we need it.

Approaches are made by telephone and by a consultant, which on this search means Jeffrey Patterson and James Grant, against the wording James Grant circulated before the session and which the room approved without change. Jason Bell continues research calls but makes no formal approach. No candidate name leaves the engagement file, and the client sees roles and records until the slate is presented.
The next working session is triggered rather than diarised: we reconvene when eight of the fourteen have been reached, whether or not all eight have answered.
Reservations recorded

Jeffrey Patterson asked that his reservation be minuted, which is that fourteen is a thin field for a seat with this much financial specificity, and that if four of the fourteen decline we will be short of a slate and back at the map with a month gone. Jennifer Frazier accepted the risk in the room and said the board will take a short slate over a padded one, and she asked only that we tell her the week we know rather than the week we are due to report.

I record a reservation of my own. Two of the fourteen sit at companies close enough to the client's market that an approach could be read as a conflict by their own boards, and I have asked Jeffrey Patterson to put both names to Jennifer Frazier before either is called.
Items and owners

Approaches to the fourteen, in priority order
Conflict check on the two adjacent-market names
Research calls against the remaining twenty-seven

Board director search, {{fact:f:E-2017-001.client}}: progress report

Prepared by: Jason Bell, Research Associate
Period: since the working session
Where we are

The search is on schedule. All fourteen priority approaches are out, ahead of the two weeks the working session allowed for them, and eleven have produced a conversation. Four of those eleven are people we would put in front of the board.

The pattern in the responses is worth stating early. Candidates with the financial background answer quickly and ask hard questions about time; candidates with the operating background answer slowly and ask about the board itself. That has shaped how the second conversations are being set up.
Nothing this period has changed the specification or the fee. The slate is the next piece of work and the schedule now turns on it.
Done this period

items: 1. Fourteen approaches completed. Jeffrey Patterson made ten and James Grant made four, all by telephone and all against the approved wording.
2. Eleven conversations held. Three of the fourteen have not responded. They stay on the list and we will try each once more before we treat the approach as closed.
3. Three declines recorded with reasons. Two cited the time the committee work would take. One is taking a seat elsewhere this year and told us so directly.
4. Four candidates carried forward. Each has read the specification and each has agreed to a second conversation.
5. Four candidates still in conversation, undecided in either direction. Two of the four are the more interesting profiles on the list, which is the usual pattern at this stage.
6. Conflict check cleared on the two names sitting in adjacent markets. Neither raised an objection from the client side and both have now been approached.
7. Research calls continued against the twenty-seven names behind the fourteen, so that a second wave can go out inside a week if it is needed.

blocks.text: In progress

Second conversations with the four carried candidates are being scheduled now. James Grant runs them and writes each candidate up against the specification, point by point, so the board reads assessments in a common format rather than four different arguments. Two of the four have asked to meet a sitting director before they go further, which is a reasonable request at this level and one we would like the board to accommodate.

The slate document is in draft. It describes each candidate by current role and record, as agreed, with names disclosed in the room when the slate is presented. Reference work is prepared but not started; we take references on finalists only and only with consent, and no reference call goes out while a candidate is still weighing the seat.
The second wave is drafted and idle. Six names from the remaining twenty-seven are ready to approach, with wording already cleared, and they go out the day the board tells us the field is too narrow.
We have asked for a date for the slate session. Jeffrey Patterson is working with your office on it.
Budget

The search is a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2017-001.fee}} and that figure is unchanged. Two of the three installments will have been invoiced by the time the slate is presented, in line with the engagement letter. Expenses to date are candidate travel for one conversation held in person, billed at cost and immaterial against the fee. No work has been done outside the scope of the engagement letter and none is contemplated.
Risks

items: 1. The field is narrow. Four carried candidates is a slate, but not a comfortable one, and two withdrawals would send us back to the map. We are holding a second wave of names ready and can approach them inside a week.

2. The chair question is still open. Candidates ask it, and for two of the four carried candidates the answer will matter to their decision. We are approaching on committee membership and describing the chair as undecided, which is accurate but not persuasive.

3. Calendars later in the summer. Two of the four carried candidates travel, and board diaries thin out at the same time. We have asked for the slate session date now, ahead of the write-ups, so that the date is held whatever the assessments say.

4. The adjacent-market question is cleared but not closed. Both names were approached with the client's agreement, and both asked how an overlap would be handled if their own boards raised it. That answer has to come from the client, and it will be needed before either could accept the seat.

blocks.text: Next report

The next report follows the slate presentation and carries the assessment summaries with it. It will also carry the reference plan for whichever candidates the board takes forward, so that the timetable to appointment is visible in one place. If the board wants a read before then, Jeffrey Patterson can give it on a call at a day's notice.
